### The Elusive Asian Giant Softshell Turtle

The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*), also known as Cantor's Giant Softshell Turtle, is one of the world's largest and most unusual freshwater turtles. Resembling a flattened, olive-green pancake with a leathery carapace instead of a hard shell, this reptile is a master of camouflage. Its most distinct features are its broad head, tiny eyes set close to a short, snorkel-like snout, and a wide, frog-like mouth, earning it the nickname "frog-faced turtle."

![A close-up of the Asian Giant Softshell Turtle's head, showing its snorkel-like snout.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Pelochelys_cantorii_-_Kaeng_Krachan.jpg/1280px-Pelochelys_cantorii_-_Kaeng_Krachan.jpg)

This remarkable turtle is an ambush predator, spending up to 95% of its life buried motionless in the sand or mud of slow-moving rivers and estuaries across Southeast Asia. With only its eyes and snout exposed, it waits patiently for unsuspecting prey like fish, crustaceans, and mollusks to swim by before lunging out with surprising speed. It surfaces only twice a day to breathe. Adults can reach over three feet in length and weigh more than 220 pounds (100 kg).

Sadly, this unique species is critically endangered. According to the IUCN Red List, its population is in severe decline due to a combination of threats. The primary pressures are habitat loss from dam construction and sand dredging, which destroy the turtle's nesting and basking sites. Furthermore, they are extensively harvested for their meat and eggs, which are considered a delicacy in many regions. Conservation efforts are underway, including breeding programs and habitat protection along key river systems like the Mekong. In fact, the turtle was thought to be extinct in Cambodia until it was rediscovered in 2007, highlighting the urgent need to protect the remaining populations of this elusive giant.

![A full-body view of the Asian Giant Softshell Turtle showing its flat, leathery shell.](https://www.asianturtleprogram.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/170327-pelochelys-cantorii-25-1080x675.jpeg)

***

### Bibliography

Langley, Liz. “This Bizarre Turtle Has a Built-In Snorkel and a Taste for Blood.” *National Geographic*, 22 Feb. 2019, www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/article/bizarre-cantors-giant-softshell-turtle-rediscovered.

“WCS ‘Rediscovers’ Elusive Giant Turtle in Cambodia.” *WCS Newsroom*, Wildlife Conservation Society, 16 May 2007, newsroom.wcs.org/News-Releases/articleType/ArticleView/articleId/362/WCS-Rediscovers-Elusive-Giant-Turtle-in-Cambodia.aspx.
